summary.text: A 72-year-old man presented with six months of progressive, painless right cervical and left inguinal swelling, with firm, non-tender, mobile nodes of 3 × 2 cm and 2.5 × 1.5 cm on examination. Constitutional symptoms were denied in the case presentation, and no tuberculosis exposure or recent infections were reported.

Workup showed mild anemia with hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL, elevated ESR, ultrasonographic hepatosplenomegaly, mesenteric lymphadenopathy and minimal ascites, thyroid nodules, and CT lymph node enlargement with mild pleural effusion raising suspicion for lymphoma. FNAC of the left inguinal node suggested tubercular lymphadenitis, so excisional biopsies were performed.

Microscopy showed Reed–Sternberg cells in an inflammatory background with granulomas, and immunohistochemistry was CD15 positive, partially CD20 positive and CD45 negative, confirming classical Hodgkin lymphoma. Bone marrow biopsy excluded marrow infiltration. Ann Arbor stage is reported inconsistently as IIIB in the abstract and Stage II in the text.

He was referred to oncologic care and started on standard ABVD chemotherapy, with an interim PET-CT planned after two cycles and results awaited. Healing after surgery progressed well without adverse events, he was compliant, and future follow-up appointments were planned.
